title: CRE PAPER 2 FORM
text:
313/2
 CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION PAPER 2
 MARKING SCHEME
 1. (a) Outline Nathan’s prophesy about the Messiah 2 Samuel (7:3-17)
 - Nathan prophesied that a heir from David’s lineage would be raised to sit on the throne.
 - Nathan prophesied that a king would deliver and save his people.
 - Nathan prophesied that God would ensure that the kingdom of God would be everlasting.
 - The Messiah would be a descendant of David.
 - The Messiah would be like a son of God.
 - He would deliver Israel from her political enemies.
 - God would keep the Messiah’s kingdom strong.
 𝟕 × 𝟏 = 𝟕𝒎𝒌𝒔
 (b) The role of John the Baptist as a fore-runner of Jesus Christ.
 - He condemned King Herod for marrying his brother’s wife.
 - He bore witness to Jesus as the Messiah.
 - He told soldiers to be contented with their wages.
 - He advised the rich to share with the poor.
 - He baptized people as a sign of repentance.
 - He Baptist Jesus at River Jordan.
 - He ushered people to the Messianic error.
 - He preached repentance of sin.
 - He warned people of the coming judgement.
 - He told tax collectors not to collect what was illegal.
 𝟕 × 𝟏 = 𝟕𝒎𝒌𝒔
 (c) State six reasons why Christians find it difficult to apply John’s teachings.
 - They lack faith in God’s word.
 - Discrimination in the church i.e. along tribal lines affects their unity.
 - Inability to abandon their past sinful lives.
 - Negative attitudes by the rich towards the poor.
 - Influence from mass media/societal moral decadence.
 - Due to rampant corruption in the society.
 - Lack of role models in the society.
 - Some Christians lead hypocritical life styles.
 𝟔 × 𝟏 = 𝟔𝒎𝒌𝒔
 2. (a) Describe the raising of Jairus daughter in (Luke 8:40-56)
 - Jairus who was a ruler in the synagogue came and fell at Jesus feet.
 - He begged Jesus to accompany him to his house and heal his 12 years old daughter who was ill.
 - Before Jesus was reached, word came that the daughter was already dead and that he should not trouble
 Jesus.
 - Jesus told Jairus to have faith in him and all would be well.
 - On arrival to Jairus home, Jesus told the mourners not to wail as the girl was only asleep.
 - Jesus together with Peter, John and James and parents of the girl entered into the house.
 - Jesus held the girl hands, saying, “Child arise”.
 - Her spirit returned to her.
 - Jesus then ordered her parents to give her something to eat.
 - The parents were amazed.
 - Jesus commanded them not to tell anyone what had happened.
 𝟕 × 𝟏 = 𝟕𝒎𝒌𝒔
 (b) State seven reactions of people towards the miracles of Jesus. 𝟕𝒎𝒌𝒔
 - Feared seized them
 - Wonder
 - Their faith was restored
 - Astonishment
 - Thanksgiving/glorification of God
 - Forgiveness
 - Abuse and rejection
 - Amazement
 - Doubting the source of Jesus power.
 - Hostility/animosity
 (c) How does the church continue with the healing ministry of Jesus Christ. 𝟔𝒎𝒌𝒔
 - Praying/preaching to the sick.
 - Laying hands on the sick/anointing them/performing any act of miracle.
 - Provision of guidelines and counseling sessions.
 - Constructing hospitals/health centers/rehabilitation.
 - Providing preventive/curative drugs/treating the sick.
 - Paying medical expenses for the sick.
 - Preaching against evil/cause of ailments which interfere with good health.
 - Providing food, clothing and shelter to the sick.
 - Visiting the sick to comfort them.
 - Training medical personnel/establishing medical training institutes.
 - Provision of civil education through seminaries/worships.
 - Providing literature/electronic media on health issues.
 𝟔 × 𝟏 = 𝟔𝒎𝒌𝒔
 3. (a) Explains the teachings of Jesus about the eschatology as recorded in St. Lukes Gospel.
 𝟔𝒎𝒌𝒔
 - People will come claiming to be the Messiah.
 - Nations will be in despair.
 - Occurrence of natural calamities e.g. earthquakes, famine
 - Destruction of the temple and the city of Jerusalem.
 - Persecution of Jesus followers.
 - Appearance of celestial beings in the sky.
 - The sea will roar.
 - People will faint from fear of witnessing signs.
 (b) Outline 7 ways in which Jesus gives hope to Christians. 𝟔𝒎𝒌𝒔
 - Through the resurrection Jesus, Christians are assured of the life after death.
 - During his mission he dealt with non-Jews giving Christians hope that he came for all.
 - During his baptism, he was confirmed by God as the expected Messiah.
 - Through teaching his disciples how to pray, Christians can also ask God for what they need through prayers.
 - Jesus chose people of low class to be his disciples, to Christians this implies that the kingdom of God is
 meant for all.
 - Through his death on the cross he brought salvation to all human beings.
 - He fed 5,000 assuring Christians of God’s providence always.
 - Jesus promised his disciples a helper (Holy Spirit)
 - Christians also do ask guidance from the Holy Spirit.
 - Through overcoming temptations in the desert, we gives hope to Christians that they can also overcome any
 obstacles in their Christian lives.
 - Through his healing miracles, he liberated those suffering spiritually and physically. Christians can also be
 liberated from all their sufferings.
 (c) Highlight 6 ways on how Christians should prepare themselves for the second coming of Jesus
 Christ. 𝟔𝒎𝒌𝒔
 - Through reading the bible.
 - Praying and fasting
 - Constantly believing in Jesus Christ as savour and Lord.
 - Attending fellowship
 - Living holy lives by avoiding sin.
 - Helping the needy
 - Evangelizing
 4. (a) State five symbolic expressions used in teaching unity of believe. 𝟓𝒎𝒌𝒔
 - The body of Christ
 - The vine and the branches
 - The people of God
 - The bride
 - The church
 (b)
 - They met for prayers/prayed together.
 - They shared their belongings/property.
 - They sold their property and distributed the money.
 - They celebrated the Holy Communion.
 - They helped the less fortunate.
 - They welcomed each other to their homes.
 - They solved problems affecting the church.
 - Churches in one need sent help to churches that were in need.
 - They prayed for one another.
 𝟖 × 𝟏 = 𝟖𝒎𝒌𝒔
 (c) State seven ways in which Christian can promote unity in the church today. 𝟕𝒎𝒌𝒔
 - By holding joint/interdenominational prayers.
 - Taking a common stand against abuse of justice/condemn sin.
 - Should promote educational standards.
 - Respect one another’s faith/religion.
 - Promote love to all in the church.
 - By avoiding discrimination/nepotism/tribalism.
 - By avoiding politics in the church.
 - By sharing/helping the needy.
 - Caring for the health of the members/building homes for the destitute.
 5. (a) Outline 5 basic of Christian ethics. 𝟓𝒎𝒌𝒔
 - The bible
 - Natural laws
 - Human reason and experience
 - Situation ethics
 - Church laws
 - Free will
 - State laws
 (b) Give seven reasons why some marriages are not formalized in Kenya. 𝟕𝒎𝒌𝒔
 - Due to financial constrain, most couple cannot cater for their wedding expenses.
 - Some couple elopes without formalizing their marriage due to cultural differences.
 - Some couples involved in demanding duties may spend most of their time in their duties other than their
 marital issues.
 - Some couples doesn’t like publicity hence may decide not to formalize their marriage.
 - Fear of the consequences of declaring the marriage that is some parents may be against a marriage leading
 one not to formalize a marriage.
 - Some fear responsibility such as paying the dowry hence may not formalize their marriage.
 - Some do not formalize their marriage because they think they may discover something from their partners
 later hence would rather live without formalizing their marriage.
 6. (a) Reasons why its important to have laws in a country.
 - Safeguards peoples rights.
 - Protect consumer from exploitation.
 - Provides for economic growth/development
 - Individuals enjoy freedom of worship.
 - Acts as a measure of those in authority.
 - Outlines how foreigners should be howled.
 - Control taxation
 (b) Explain the Christian teaching on work. 𝟖𝒎𝒌𝒔
 - All people must work as God himself also worked.
 - Work is not a curse as man was created to work.
 - Work is essential to man’s and the states developments.
 - Man works to avoid idleness which is condemned in the bible.
 - The bible recognizes labour specialization because God gave people different talents.
 - Paul teaches that work accords one dignity e.g. he was a tent maker.
 - Paul says that whoever does not work should not eat.
 - Work glorifies God.
 - Work is a social human activity.
 - Christians work for self-reliance and independent.
 𝟖 × 𝟏 = 𝟖𝒎𝒌𝒔
 (c) How the church is helping to reduce the rate of crime.
 - Providing guidance and counseling.
 - Preaching about love for one another.
 - Rehabilitating law breakers.
 - Providing jobs.
 - Giving loans
 - Providing recreational activities for the youth.
 - Reporting criminals
 - Disciplining deviant members of the church.
 - Obeying laws of the country.
 - Providing basic needs for the needy.
